verdict: Clorox sales jumped 33% to $1.9B as retailers rebuilt inventories after last year's ERP disruption and the newly bought GOJO business added about 15 points of growth, more than doubling EPS to $1.39.

segments.note: Cleaning products and professional products — now including GOJO, the maker of Purell hand sanitizer, which contributed about 39 points of this segment's 62% growth.

segments.note: Glad bags and wraps, Fresh Step cat litter and Kingsford grilling — growth was all volume, as retailers restocked after the ERP drawdown.

footerNote: Clorox's fiscal year ends June 30, so this is Q1 of fiscal 2027. The flow uses total net earnings of $173M; after $3M attributable to noncontrolling interests, net earnings attributable to Clorox were $170M ($1.39 per diluted share). Operating income of $261M is gross profit less selling & administrative, advertising and R&D, as presented in Clorox's statement of earnings.

takeaways.title: A rebound quarter, flattered by last year
takeaways.text: About 18 points of the growth was organic — mostly retailers rebuilding stock after drawing down inventories during last year's ERP system transition, a one-off drag Clorox is now lapping. GOJO added roughly 15 points more.

takeaways.title: GOJO changes the shape of Clorox
takeaways.text: Health and Wellness is now 48% of all sales after the GOJO deal brought Purell's professional hygiene business in-house. Integrating it — and paying down the debt taken on — is the story of the next few quarters.

takeaways.title: Costs are still biting
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 130 basis points to 40.4% on higher commodity, manufacturing and logistics costs — including about 50 basis points from writing up GOJO's inventory to fair value. Cost savings and volume only partly offset it.

oneTimers: GOJO transaction costs — mainly integration spending and the inventory step-up (writing acquired stock up to fair value, which then flows through cost of sales) — weighed on GAAP results; excluding them and similar items, adjusted EPS was $1.55 vs the $1.39 GAAP figure.

The year-ago quarter was depressed by retailers drawing down inventory built up ahead of Clorox's ERP system transition — Clorox estimates that comparison added about $0.90 to this quarter's EPS growth rate.
